questions.q: When praised for the rescue, who did Passepartout say deserved the credit?
choices: Sir Francis Cromarty
The Parsee guide
Mr. Fogg
Kiouni the elephant
questions.evidence: all the credit of the affair belonged to Mr. Fogg

questions.q: Why did Sir Francis worry about Aouda staying in India?
choices: She had no money and no family left anywhere in the country
The fanatics would find her again, even in the big cities
The English police wanted to question her about the rajah
She was too weak from the hemp fumes to travel by train
questions.evidence: would inevitably fall again into the hands of her executioners

questions.q: What was Passepartout sent to buy for Aouda in Allahabad?
choices: Clothes such as a dress, shawl and furs
Medicine and food for the train journey
A ticket for the steamer to Hong Kong
A trunk and a travelling-blanket
questions.evidence: a dress, shawl, and some furs

questions.q: Fogg gave Passepartout "unlimited credit" for the shopping. What does this mean?
choices: He could only spend a few pounds and had to bring back change
He could spend as much as he needed
He had to borrow the money from a bank in the city
He must pay with his own wages and be paid back later
questions.evidence: his master gave him unlimited credit

questions.q: Allahabad is built where two sacred rivers meet. Which two?
choices: The Indus and the Ganges
The Ganges and the Jumna
The Jumna and the Hugly
The Nile and the Ganges
questions.evidence: the two sacred rivers, Ganges and Jumna

questions.q: Why did it surprise Passepartout that Fogg paid the guide only the agreed price?
choices: The guide had risked his life and might face revenge for helping
The guide had asked to be paid twice the agreed price at the very start
Fogg usually paid every servant much more than he owed
The guide had also bought the clothes for Aouda himself
questions.evidence: He had, indeed, risked his life in the adventure at Pillaji

questions.q: What reward did Fogg give the guide for his devotion?
choices: A purse of fifty pounds
The elephant Kiouni
His gold pocket watch
A free ticket to Calcutta
questions.evidence: Would you like to have this elephant? He is yours.

questions.q: What did Fogg mean when he said, "I have paid for your service, but not for your devotion"?
choices: The guide's loyalty was worth more than his wages, so he deserved a gift
The guide had not finished the whole job, so he would not get the full price
The guide still owed Fogg money for the damage to the pagoda
The guide should work for Fogg for the rest of the journey
questions.evidence: I have paid for your service, but not for your devotion.

questions.q: What did Kiouni do after Passepartout fed him lumps of sugar?
choices: He knelt down so Passepartout could climb on his back
He lifted Passepartout with his trunk and set him down gently
He trumpeted loudly and ran off toward the forest
He followed Passepartout onto the station platform
questions.evidence: lifted him as high as his head

questions.q: How did Aouda feel when she woke up on the train?
choices: Happy to be going home to Bombay
Astonished to be among strangers in European clothes
Angry that she had been taken from the pagoda
Calm, because she remembered everything that happened
questions.evidence: What was her astonishment to find herself in this carriage

questions.q: Where did Fogg offer to take Aouda so she would be safe?
choices: To Calcutta, where the English police could guard her
To Bombay, to the home of her late father
To Hong Kong, where she had a relative who was a merchant
To London, to live safely in his own house on Saville Row
questions.evidence: offered, in order to reassure her, to escort her to Hong Kong

questions.q: Which companion left the group when the train reached Benares?
choices: The Parsee guide
Sir Francis Cromarty
Aouda
Passepartout
questions.evidence: Benares was Sir Francis Cromarty's destination

questions.q: Why would Passepartout have liked to see Chandernagor in daylight?
choices: It was the town where he had been born and raised
It was a French town where he hoped to see his country's flag
It had the most famous rose-water factories anywhere in all of India
His old fire brigade had once been stationed there
questions.evidence: Passepartout would have been proud to see his country's flag flying

questions.q: How did Fogg's arrival in Calcutta compare to the plan in his journal?
choices: He arrived two days early, thanks to the elephant
He arrived on exactly the date he had planned
He arrived one day late because of the rescue
He arrived a week early and had to wait for the ship
questions.evidence: that was the exact date of his actual arrival

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: The journey from the pagoda across India to Calcutta with Aouda
Fogg's arrest by the police as soon as he reaches Calcutta
Passepartout's long tour of the city of Allahabad alone
Sir Francis and Fogg playing whist on the train to Bombay
questions.evidence: Calcutta was reached at seven in the morning
